newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Parent to privatise East Asiatic (H.K.).
newsitem.headline: Parent to privatise East Asiatic (H.K.).

text.p: East Asiatic Co (Hong Kong) Ltd said on Friday its Danish parent the East Asiatic Co Ltd had put forward a proposal to privatise the Hong Kong company, valuing the unit at HK$520 million.

The two companies said in a joint statement that the parent proposed to buy the Hong Kong unit's shares at HK$1.30 each, or for the equivalent number of shares in the parent which are listed on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange.
The price will represent a 154.9 percent premium to the audited consolidated net asset value per share of about HK$0.51 as at December 31, 1996, the statement said.
The Hong Kong company shares ended at HK$1.18 each on Monday prior to a trading suspension. Trading in its shares is due to resume on Friday.

"Upon completion of the proposal, the company will be wholly owned by the parent company and the company will apply to The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Ltd for the withdrawal of the listing of the shares on the Stock Exchange," it said.
The Hong Kong listed company is 75 percent controlled by The East Asiatic Co (Hong Kong) Holdings Ltd, which is a wholly-owned unit of the Danish parent.
